newsitem.title: USA: Agouron sells Asian rights to Viracept.
newsitem.headline: Agouron sells Asian rights to Viracept.

text.p: Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc and Japan Tobacco Inc said Tuesday they sold Asian marketing rights for the AIDS drug Viracept to Roche Holding Ltd's Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd division
Under the terms of the deal, Roche will pay Japan Tobacco and Agouron a total of $6 million plus royalties on Roche's sales of Viracept.

The agreement also provides for Roche to seek approval for Viracept in several Asian countries including China, India, Turkey, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam. Roche will immediately pay the companies $4 million, to be shared equally, and will pay the additional $2 million when Viracept is first approved in one of those Asian countries.

Viracept, being developed by Agouron and the pharmaceutical division of Japan Tobacco, belongs to a class of AIDS drugs known as protease inhibitors. These drugs have been shown to dramatically reduce viral load in some patients when they are combined with two other AIDS drugs. Viracept was approved in the U.S. earlier this year.
